newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Lenenergo resumes payment of wages.
newsitem.headline: Lenenergo resumes payment of wages.

text.p: Russian power utility AOOT Lenenergo has started paying wages again, averting the risk of its workers taking strike action, the president of the company's union council said on Monday.
"Our appeal to the authorities obviously had an effect and at the end of last week the company's accounts were unblocked and people began to receive their wages," Georgi Turlov told Reuters.
The union threatened to take industrial action after the tax office froze Lenenergo's accounts on September 19 in order to write off the company's tax debts.

Lenergo failed to pay taxes after customers failed to pay for their electricity -- a typical situation in Russia where companies and individuals often become locked in a web of non-payment due to their financial difficulties.
"I hope that tensions will die down after wages start being paid, though there is still a mood of dissatisfaction in the collective," Turlov said.
AO Lenenergo comprises 36 enterprises employing 18,000 workers.
